tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

# CLAUDE.md — Spend Radar (neatHack 2026)

You are building **Spend Radar** with Akarsh (team **qwep**, solo) for **neatHack**, a 48-hour online AI-agent hackathon run by neatlogs. This file is the full brief: the rules, the scoring, what to build, the order to build it, and what evidence to produce. Read all of it before writing code. Re-read "Hard rules" whenever you are unsure.

Source of rules: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (fetched 10 Oct 2026). Build-log skill: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill. If anything here conflicts with those pages, the pages win; tell Akarsh.

---

## 0. Hard rules (breaking any of these can disqualify us or cost money)

1. **All code is written during the hackathon**: Sat 10 Oct 2026, 12:30 PM IST → Mon 12 Oct 2026, 11:55 PM IST. Do not copy in code from any earlier project, including Akarsh's other repos (Glance, SecureAgent, etc.). Open-source libraries installed via pip/npm are fine.
2. **Public GitHub repo**, with commits made throughout the event so judges can see the dates. Commit small and often (at least every hour of work). Never squash or rewrite history. The repo's first commit must be after 12:30 PM IST, 10 Oct.
3. **Must use all three: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai**, each with a clear role, and the demo must cover all three.
4. **Demo video ≤ 3 minutes** (not stated on the rules page; we keep it as the safe limit).
5. **Submission** = a public quote-post on X of the official neatlogs submission post, between **Mon 12 Oct, 7:00 PM and 11:55 PM IST**, containing team name (qwep), project name, public repo link, demo link. Late = not judged.
6. **Do not use Glance** or any of Akarsh's existing projects in this repo.
7. **No fabricated numbers anywhere** — not in code, README, report, posts, or the video. Every confidence score is computed. Every metric comes from a saved scorecard or trace link. Unmeasured numbers in drafts are written as `{N}` placeholders and filled only from a real run. Estimates are labelled as estimates.
8. **Never commit secrets.** `.env` (git-ignored) plus `.env.example`. Secrets never appear in commits, logs, neatlogs traces, or screenshots (see §6.1).
9. **Zero spend, everywhere.** No billing on any service. Free tiers only for LLMs (§3). Never add credits or a payment method to OpenRouter, Google AI Studio, or anything else. cfo.ai is cancelled in Settings → Billing immediately after signup. AWS use stays inside the organisers' allowance and instances are stopped whenever idle. Anything that could incur a charge → ask Akarsh first.
10. **Real customer finance data never goes through free LLM providers.** We only send fictional Acme data and public Crustdata facts.

---

## 1. Judging (optimise for this, in this order)

| Category | Weight | What the judges look at |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | How well the agent handles a substantial task start to finish |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | How effectively they were used to build, improve, and plan a business around the agent |
| Demo video | 20% | How clearly it explains the agent and the use of all three tools |
| Building in public | 15% | What was shared publicly during the hackathon, tagged #neatHack |
| Usefulness & originality | 10% | A real problem solved in a new way |

Focus areas for the agent: **planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification, iteration**. The design must visibly hit every one.

**Evidence judges require (each claim must be checkable):**
- *Agent improved*: runs before and after a change (neatlogs traces) with numbers compared (§7).
- *Used neatlogs*: trace links or screenshots.
- *Used Entire*: checkpoints or entire-graph output from the repo.
- *Used cfo.ai*: a business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, runway.
- *Recovers from failure*: a run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next.
- *Built in public*: links to posts tagged #neatHack.
- *Wrote code during hackathon*: public repo with dated commits.

Judges: 2 from Entire (devrel, solutions engineer), 2 from neatlogs (founder, head of product engineering), 1 founder of Orchestrator.inc. They build agent/dev tooling. They will notice fake metrics and will appreciate real traces, real bugs found and fixed, and clean engineering.

Prizes: 1st $2,000 + $5,000 Dodo credits; 2nd $1,000 + $3,000; 3rd $500 + $1,000; each winner gets 3 months neatlogs Pro. Separate $500 community award for genuine community interest. Winners announced 16 Oct.

---

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

**Problem:** Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They learn a competitor doubled its ML team or raised a round a quarter late.

**The task the agent completes end to end:**
> Input: a folder of the company's finance files (budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, spend policy) and a hard-coded competitor list (`data/acme/competitors.yaml`).
> Output: a report per spend category with our actual spend, the competitor estimate range, the gap, whether policy is violated, a recommendation, and a link to every source behind every number — plus a list of claims the agent checked and overturned.

**Category scope (decided):**
- **Competitor comparison is on people cost only**: engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing *team*. Each category states "people cost only" in the report. Policy rules in `policy.yaml` are written against people cost.
- **Infra/cloud** is checked only internally (our invoices vs budget vs policy). No competitor estimate for it.

**Competitors:** real dev-tools / AI-infra companies. Step 1 probes 7 candidates — Datadog, Grafana Labs, Chronosphere, Honeycomb, Arize, New Relic, Sentry — and keeps the 4–5 with the best Crustdata coverage. Never include neatlogs or Entire (their people judge). Competitor auto-selection is a stretch goal only.

**Our company:** "Acme Observability Inc." — fictional, labelled as such everywhere.

---

## 3. Tool stack and the role of each tool

| Job | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trace every LLM call, tool call, retry, decision, state change; find bugs; compare runs | **neatlogs** (required) | Docs: https://docs.neatlogs.com, https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk. Integrate before agent logic so the first run is traced. Details in §6. |
| Repo context and checkpoints for the coding agent (you) | **Entire** (required) | Already enabled for Claude Code (`entire enable --agent claude-code`; re-run after any `git init`). Checkpoints add an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer to commits. Evidence: `entire checkpoint list/explain`, `entire graph stats`, entire-graph output → `evidence/entire/`. |
| Business plan: pricing, costs, revenue, runway | **cfo.ai** (required) | Akarsh signs up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks and cancels the subscription immediately. He builds the model; you prepare inputs (§9). |
| Competitor data | **Crustdata** | 5,000 credits. Auth: `authorization: Bearer <key>`, `x-api-version: 2025-11-01`. `POST /company/enrich` (`fields`: headcount incl. `by_role_absolute`/`by_role_percent`, growth `mom/qoq/six_months/yoy/two_years`; funding) ≈ 2 credits/company. `POST /job/search` (`job_details.title`, `job_details.category`, `metadata.date_added`; `group_by` aggregations, `limit:0` for aggregation-only) at 0.03 credits/result. No headcount timeseries — trend comes from growth fields. Confirm all fields with the Step 1 probe; check real prices via `GET /account/endpoints`. |
| LLM — primary | **Google Gemini, free tier only** (`google-genai>=1.55.0`) | Role split: Pro → plan, `decide:recovery`, self-audit; Flash → report prose; Flash-Lite → extraction, title classification, JSON re-asks. **Read the real model list and rate limits from AI Studio in Step 2; do not trust model names from memory.** If Pro's daily quota is too small, the eval decides whether Flash is good enough for planning (becomes a case study). |
| LLM — secondary | **OpenRouter, `:free` models only** | Never add credits. A guard in `llm.py` refuses any model ID not ending in `:free`. Free limits without credits: 20 req/min, 50 req/day. Roles: (1) cross-provider failover after Gemini retries + model fallback are exhausted; (2) independent second opinion in the self-audit, max 5 calls/run, only on findings Gemini marked uncertain or overturned. Pick the model in Step 2 by listing free models via the API; it must support JSON output or tool calling and pass our Pydantic schemas. |
| Hosting (optional) | **AWS** | Organisers' allowance ($25, us-east-1 only) covers EC2, Lambda, IAM and load balancers only; Bedrock is not available. One instance, t3.micro or t3.small, in Hackathon_VPC, for a live report / scheduled runs. Stop it whenever not needed (the access page does not track spend). Never on the critical path. AWS keys stay in `.env` and never appear in commits, logs, traces or screenshots. |
| File parsing | `openpyxl` (xlsx), `pdfplumber` (PDF), Gemini PDF input as fallback for scanned PDFs | Test both PDF routes early; keep the one that works. |
| Language | Python 3.11+, plain hand-written loop, Pydantic for state | No heavy agent framework. |

All LLM calls go through one module, `llm.py`: `llm(role=..., ...)` picks the model per role, enforces the `:free` guard, the rate limiter, and the quota ledger, and records provider/model on every span.

---

## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.

**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).

### 4.2 Tools

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

### 4.3 State and resumability

- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.

### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)

- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.

### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)

1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.

**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.

### 4.6 Budgets and quotas

- **Crustdata:** cap 60 credits per run; never more than 100 credits in one go without asking Akarsh.
- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.

---

## 5. Build order (commit after each numbered step)

All times IST. If behind schedule, see §11.

### Saturday 10 Oct — working skeleton by midnight

**Step 0 (before 12:30, no code):** Akarsh does web check-in, Luma, Discord, cfo.ai signup + immediate cancel. Plan and read docs only.

**Step 1 — Repo + Crustdata spike (12:30–1:15, ≤ 25 credits):**
- Reset local git (the pre-12:30 `.git` is discarded — confirm with Akarsh before deleting), `git init`, re-run `entire enable --agent claude-code`, push to a new empty public repo. First commit: this CLAUDE.md, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`.
- `spikes/crustdata_probe.py`: enrich + jobs `group_by job_details.category` (`limit:0`) for the 7 candidates; raw JSON to `cache/`. Report exactly which fields exist. Pick the 4–5 best-covered → `data/acme/competitors.yaml`.
- **Decision by 2:00 PM:** role-level headcount exists → use directly; only totals + titles → `classify_titles` + 30-title labelled eval set; neither usable → stop and tell Akarsh.

**Step 2 — Instrumentation + providers (by 2:30, may run to 3:00):**
- neatlogs `init()` with `instrumentations=["google_genai"]`, the `mask` callback (§6.1), and run tags. One traced dummy Gemini call visible in the dashboard. Check whether `neatlogs sharing` can produce public trace links; if not, evidence uses screenshots.
- List real Gemini models + rate limits from AI Studio; list OpenRouter `:free` models via API and pick one that passes our schemas. Write the limits into `config.yaml` and the ledger.
- Secret-masking unit test passes (required before Step 2 counts as done).
- gitleaks pre-commit hook (§6.1), added alongside Entire's hooks; verify the Entire checkpoint trailer still appears.
- **Plan the case studies:** from the real quotas, work out how many before/after comparisons (n=3 runs per side, §7) fit in the remaining days, and write that plan into `hackathon.md` before running any.

**Step 3 — Sample data (by 4:00):** under `data/acme/` (fictional, labelled):
- `budget_fy27.xlsx` — spend by category × month
- `invoices/` — 12–15 PDFs incl. **one scanned-image PDF, one corrupt file, one whose line items don't sum to its total, one mis-categorised**
- `policy.yaml` — people-cost rules, e.g. "ML/AI team cost within 20% of competitor median"
- `salary_table.csv` — loaded cost per role category (cite a public source or label as assumption)
- `competitors.yaml` — from Step 1
- `ground_truth.json` — planted errors and correct totals (evals only, never shown to the agent)

**Step 4 — Tools (by 7:00):** §4.2 tools + `llm.py`, unit tests for the deterministic ones.

**Step 5 — Loop + state (by 10:00):** plan → act → observe → verify → decide, state saved per step; end-to-end run with a rough report.

**Step 6 — First full traced run (by midnight):** trace link → `evidence/traces.md`. Draft post #2.

### Sunday 11 Oct — trustworthy and measurable

**Step 7 — Verification + computed confidence.**
**Step 8 — Recovery paths (§4.5):** collect natural failure traces; inject the rest; save links.
**Step 9 — Eval harness (§7):** `python -m spendradar eval [--n 3]` → scorecard.
**Step 10 — Find real bugs in neatlogs traces** (hallucinated totals, wasted retries, token blow-ups, wrong tool choice, slow spans). Fix 2–3, within the case-study plan from Step 2. Each → `evidence/case-studies/NN-<slug>.md`.
**Step 11 — Self-audit pass:** measure overturn rate on planted errors and fixtures.
**Step 12 — Resume-after-crash** (kill mid-run, resume, finish). Save trace.
**Step 13 — Cost per run:** tokens/latency per model from neatlogs for 5 runs → `business/unit_costs.md` as paid-equivalent cost (§9).
**Sunday night:** record a backup demo video.

### Monday 12 Oct — package and submit

**Step 14 (by noon):** README (§10), report polish, architecture diagram (Mermaid + PNG).
**Step 15 (by 3 PM):** cfo.ai plan finalised by Akarsh, exported to `business/`.
**Step 16 (by 5 PM):** final demo video, captioned, uploaded (YouTube unlisted or Loom), ≤ 3:00.
**Step 17 (6:30 PM):** final commit, all README links verified.
**Step 18 (7:00 PM sharp):** Akarsh quote-posts the official neatlogs post (aim for the first 50).

---

## 6. neatlogs usage (25% category — central, not decorative)

- Install `neatlogs[google-genai]`; call `neatlogs.init(...)` **before** constructing the Gemini client. OpenRouter calls get custom spans (or an instrumentation key if verified in docs).
- Trace every LLM call (prompt, response, tokens, model, provider), every tool call (`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", ...)`), every retry, every `decide:recovery`, every `fallback:<model>`, verification results, self-audit verdicts. Span kinds per https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/span-kinds.
- Span names: `plan`, `act:read_pdf`, `verify:totals`, `decide:recovery`, `fallback:<model>`, `audit:finding_<id>`, `report`.
- Tags are process-wide, so each `spendradar run` is its own process with tags `sha:<short-sha>`, `run:<run_id>`, `variant:<label>`, plus `evidence` / `inject:<...>` / `fixture` when applicable.
- neatlogs has no run-comparison feature we found; our eval scorecards store trace IDs and our table does the comparison. Use neatlogs evals/experiments features only per docs; never invent APIs.
- Every bug fix

156	## 4. Agent architecture
157	
158	### 4.1 The loop
159	
160	```
161	PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
162	                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
163	when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
164	```
165	
166	1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
167	2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
168	3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
169	4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
170	5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
171	6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
172	7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.
173	
174	**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).
175	
176	### 4.2 Tools
177	
178	| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
179	|---|---|---|
180	| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
181	| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
182	| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
183	| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
184	| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
185	| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
186	| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
187	| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
188	| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
189	| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |
190	
191	All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.
192	
193	### 4.3 State and resumability
194	
195	- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
196	- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
197	- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.
198	
199	### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)
200	
201	- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
202	- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
203	- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
204	- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
205	- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.
206	
207	### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)
208	
209	1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
210	2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
211	3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
212	4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
213	5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
214	6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.
215	
216	**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.
217	
218	### 4.6 Budgets and quotas
219	
220	- **Crustdata:** cap 60 credits per run; never more than 100 credits in one go without asking Akarsh.
221	- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
222	- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.

296	## 7. Evals (turn "it improved" into a number)
297	
298	`ground_truth.json` lists planted errors (mismatched totals, mis-categorised invoice, corrupt file) and correct category totals, plus the fault-injected fixtures.
299	
300	**Fixtures rule:** Altered fixtures are allowed only in `evals/`, and every run report labels whether it used real data or a fixture. Fixtures in `evals/fixtures/` are cached real Crustdata responses with one field changed on purpose (e.g. ML job postings × 5), each logged in `ground_truth.json`. Product runs only ever read real data. `--fixtures` refuses any folder outside `evals/`, tags the run `fixture`, and sets the report's data mode to FIXTURE.
301	
302	The eval reports:
303	- planted errors caught / total
304	- category total accuracy (abs % error)
305	- unsupported numbers in report (target 0)
306	- planted/fixture false findings overturned by self-audit / total (scored)
307	- competitor findings overturned on real data: N (no ground truth — unscored; report shows both sources side by side)
308	- title-classifier accuracy on 30 labelled titles (only if used)

# hackathon.md — Spend Radar (neatHack 2026)

## Project
Spend Radar: an agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, with a source behind every number, and tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

## Team
qwep — Akarsh Dhingra (solo)

## Stack
Python 3.12, plain agent loop, Pydantic · neatlogs (tracing) · Entire (checkpoints + entire-graph) · cfo.ai (business plan) · Crustdata (competitor data) · Gemini free tier + OpenRouter `:free` models (LLM)

## Build log

### 2026-10-10 (Sat)

  - Tests run: none yet (no code).
- **13:35 IST — Step 1 done.** Crustdata probe: 28 credits (14 wasted on a duplicate enrich; fixed). All 7 candidates have role-level headcount, timeseries, funding, news; Chronosphere lacks hiring data; no ML/AI role exists, so ML/AI uses title classification. Competitors: Honeycomb, Sentry, Arize, Chronosphere, Grafana Labs (see `spikes/FINDINGS.md`).
  - Tests run: probe script against live API (7 enrich, 7 job aggregations).

Finding: Gemini Pro has zero free-tier quota → Flash plans.
  - Tests run: `pytest` 7 passed (mask, guard, ledger-not-polluted-by-injection); live probes `spikes/neatlogs_probe.py`, `spikes/llm_probe.py`.
  - Bug found and fixed: injected 429s were marking real models exhausted in the ledger.

- **13:43 IST — Step 3 done.** `scripts/make_acme_data.py` (seeded) generates the fictional Acme folder: budget xlsx (People + NonPeople), 13 invoices from invented vendors, policy.yaml (people-cost share-of-headcount rules + internal infra check), salary_table.csv (labelled ASSUMPTION), and `evals/ground_truth.json` with 5 planted errors (budget total mismatch, invoice total mismatch, mis-categorised invoice, scanned PDF, corrupt PDF). Contracts are cut, as agreed.

- **13:47 IST — Step 4 done.** Tools: `list_files`, `read_spreadsheet` (keeps row numbers), `read_pdf` text (pdfplumber + deterministic parse) and llm (Gemini reads PDF bytes), `crustdata_company` / `crustdata_jobs` (cache, backoff, stale-cache fallback, per-run credit cap, fault injection), `classify_titles` (Flash-Lite, schema-validated), and deterministic `analysis.py` (signals, ranges, agreement, policy compare, gap in heads/USD). Added an "other" staff row to the Acme budget so share-of-headcount is comparable with competitors' company totals.
  - Tests run: pytest 14 passed; live LLM PDF read of the scanned invoice (total 91,287, matching what is printed).
  - Bug found and fixed: Gemini 400 on the corrupt PDF crashed the process; non-retryable provider errors now become `LLMError` → `ToolError`.
- **14:05 IST — Step 5 (loop) in progress.** Agent loop with LLM plan + coverage check, per-task verification, LLM `decide:recovery` via native function calling, retry cap 3, atomic state save per step, `resume`, simulated crash flag, self-audit (recompute, sources, contradiction evidence, LLM verdict, OpenRouter second opinion), sourced Markdown report.

This run's LLM latency/tokens predate the cached-call accounting fix, so they are inflated.

# CLAUDE.md — Spend Radar (neatHack 2026)

You are building **Spend Radar** with Akarsh (team **qwep**, solo) for **neatHack**, a 48-hour online AI-agent hackathon run by neatlogs. This file is the full brief: the rules, the scoring, what to build, the order to build it, and what evidence to produce. Read all of it before writing code. Re-read "Hard rules" whenever you are unsure.

Source of rules: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (fetched 10 Oct 2026). Build-log skill: https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill. If anything here conflicts with those pages, the pages win; tell Akarsh.

---

## 0. Hard rules (breaking any of these can disqualify us or cost money)

1. **All code is written during the hackathon**: Sat 10 Oct 2026, 12:30 PM IST → Mon 12 Oct 2026, 11:55 PM IST. Do not copy in code from any earlier project, including Akarsh's other repos (Glance, SecureAgent, etc.). Open-source libraries installed via pip/npm are fine.
2. **Public GitHub repo**, with commits made throughout the event so judges can see the dates. Commit small and often (at least every hour of work). Never squash or rewrite history. The repo's first commit must be after 12:30 PM IST, 10 Oct.
3. **Must use all three: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai**, each with a clear role, and the demo must cover all three.
4. **Demo video ≤ 3 minutes** (not stated on the rules page; we keep it as the safe limit).
5. **Submission** = a public quote-post on X of the official neatlogs submission post, between **Mon 12 Oct, 7:00 PM and 11:55 PM IST**, containing team name (qwep), project name, public repo link, demo link. Late = not judged.
6. **Do not use Glance** or any of Akarsh's existing projects in this repo.
7. **No fabricated numbers anywhere** — not in code, README, report, posts, or the video. Every confidence score is computed. Every metric comes from a saved scorecard or trace link. Unmeasured numbers in drafts are written as `{N}` placeholders and filled only from a real run. Estimates are labelled as estimates.
8. **Never commit secrets.** `.env` (git-ignored) plus `.env.example`. Secrets never appear in commits, logs, neatlogs traces, or screenshots (see §6.1).
9. **Zero spend, everywhere.** No billing on any service. Free tiers only for LLMs (§3). Never add credits or a payment method to OpenRouter, Google AI Studio, or anything else. cfo.ai is cancelled in Settings → Billing immediately after signup. AWS use stays inside the organisers' allowance and instances are stopped whenever idle. Anything that could incur a charge → ask Akarsh first.
10. **Real customer finance data never goes through free LLM providers.** We only send fictional Acme data and public Crustdata facts.

---

## 1. Judging (optimise for this, in this order)

| Category | Weight | What the judges look at |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | How well the agent handles a substantial task start to finish |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | How effectively they were used to build, improve, and plan a business around the agent |
| Demo video | 20% | How clearly it explains the agent and the use of all three tools |
| Building in public | 15% | What was shared publicly during the hackathon, tagged #neatHack |
| Usefulness & originality | 10% | A real problem solved in a new way |

Focus areas for the agent: **planning, tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification, iteration**. The design must visibly hit every one.

**Evidence judges require (each claim must be checkable):**
- *Agent improved*: runs before and after a change (neatlogs traces) with numbers compared (§7).
- *Used neatlogs*: trace links or screenshots.
- *Used Entire*: checkpoints or entire-graph output from the repo.
- *Used cfo.ai*: a business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, runway.
- *Recovers from failure*: a run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next.
- *Built in public*: links to posts tagged #neatHack.
- *Wrote code during hackathon*: public repo with dated commits.

Judges: 2 from Entire (devrel, solutions engineer), 2 from neatlogs (founder, head of product engineering), 1 founder of Orchestrator.inc. They build agent/dev tooling. They will notice fake metrics and will appreciate real traces, real bugs found and fixed, and clean engineering.

Prizes: 1st $2,000 + $5,000 Dodo credits; 2nd $1,000 + $3,000; 3rd $500 + $1,000; each winner gets 3 months neatlogs Pro. Separate $500 community award for genuine community interest. Winners announced 16 Oct.

---

## 2. The product

**One-liner:** An agent that tells a finance team where competitors are outspending them on people, and shows its work — every number has a source, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting them.

**Problem:** Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They learn a competitor doubled its ML team or raised a round a quarter late.

**The task the agent completes end to end:**
> Input: a folder of the company's finance files (budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, spend policy) and a hard-coded competitor list (`data/acme/competitors.yaml`).
> Output: a report per spend category with our actual spend, the competitor estimate range, the gap, whether policy is violated, a recommendation, and a link to every source behind every number — plus a list of claims the agent checked and overturned.

**Category scope (decided):**
- **Competitor comparison is on people cost only**: engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing *team*. Each category states "people cost only" in the report. Policy rules in `policy.yaml` are written against people cost.
- **Infra/cloud** is checked only internally (our invoices vs budget vs policy). No competitor estimate for it.

**Competitors:** real dev-tools / AI-infra companies. ## 4. Agent architecture

### 4.1 The loop

```
PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY ─┬─ pass → next task
                               └─ fail → DECIDE:RECOVERY (LLM) → fix-up task → ACT
when queue empty → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT
```

1. **Plan** (LLM): reads goal, file listing, competitor list; emits a typed task list validated against a Pydantic schema. Traced as `plan`.
2. **Act** (Python): run the next task; exactly one tool call.
3. **Observe**: store the result in state *with its source* (file path + sheet/row or page; Crustdata endpoint + request id + fetch timestamp).
4. **Verify** (Python): deterministic check for that result type (§4.4).
5. **Decide:recovery** (LLM, native tool/function calling): on a failed check, choose one action from a fixed menu — `reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip` — with a one-line reason. Each decision is its own span `decide:recovery` recording the options offered and the one picked. The LLM may also decide that a surprising result warrants a new task.
6. **Self-audit**: tries to *disprove* each finding — re-checks sources, looks for a contradicting signal (headcount growth reversal, layoffs/freeze, funding timing), recomputes the number. OpenRouter second opinion on uncertain/overturned findings (≤ 5 calls). Downgraded/removed findings logged as "overturned".
7. **Report**: `runs/<run_id>/report.md` (+ `report.html` if time) with every number linked to its source, an "Overturned claims" section, and a header stating **data mode: real | fixture** and the provider mix.

**Who decides what:** the LLM decides the plan, recovery choices, and whether to add tasks. Python decides task execution, all maths, retry caps, and quota/credit limits. The demo must show at least one recovery choice that differs from the obvious default (e.g. fetching an extra signal instead of skipping).

### 4.2 Tools

| Tool | Deterministic? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `list_files(folder)` | yes | inventory inputs |
| `read_spreadsheet(path, sheet, range)` | yes | budget lines |
| `read_pdf(path, pages, mode="text"/"llm")` | text: yes; llm: no | invoices |
| `crustdata_company(name_or_domain)` | yes (API) | headcount by role, growth, funding |
| `crustdata_jobs(company, filters)` | yes (API) | open roles, grouped by `job_details.category` |
| `classify_titles(titles)` | no (LLM) | only if Crustdata categories prove unusable in Step 1 |
| `estimate_spend(headcount_by_category, salary_table)` | yes | headcount → estimated annual people cost |
| `compare(ours, theirs, policy)` | yes | gap + policy violation per category |
| `find_contradictions(finding)` | mixed | used by self-audit |
| `write_report(state)` | yes | final output |

All money/maths is deterministic Python. The LLM never does arithmetic that ends up in the report.

### 4.3 State and resumability

- One `RunState` (Pydantic) per run: goal, task queue, completed tasks, extracted figures (value + source), competitor figures (value + source), verification results, retry counts, recovery decisions, overturned findings, token/request totals per model, provider mix, data mode.
- Save to `runs/<run_id>/state.json` after **every** step. `python -m spendradar resume <run_id>` continues from the last saved step.
- Cache every Crustdata response to `cache/crustdata/<hash>.json`. Cache LLM responses to `cache/llm/` in development.

### 4.4 Verification checks (confidence is computed, never typed in)

- Spreadsheet/invoice line items sum to the stated total within 1%.
- Each invoice amount appears in the budget category it is mapped to (or is flagged).
- Each competitor estimate rests on ≥ 2 independent signals, else `low_confidence`.
- Every number in the report has a stored source; a number without one is dropped.
- `confidence = f(checks passed, number of signals, data freshness)` — implement in `verify.py`, document the formula in the README.

### 4.5 Recovery paths (each must appear in at least one saved trace)

1. Corrupt/unreadable PDF → other parser → skip and list under "Not analysed".
2. Crustdata timeout / 429 / 5xx → exponential backoff, max 3 retries → cached response if available → mark data missing.
3. Competitor with no data → substitute next-closest company, noted in report.
4. Totals mismatch → re-read with narrower range → flag the file.
5. LLM returns malformed JSON → re-ask with the validation error, max 2 times.
6. LLM 429 / 5xx → backoff → different free Gemini model (own quota) → OpenRouter `:free` model. Each hop is a `fallback:<model>` span.

**Failure traces:** save **natural** failures whenever they happen (free tiers will 429 on their own) *and* deliberate ones via a fault-injection switch, `--inject <target>:<fault>` (e.g. `crustdata:429`). Injected runs are tagged `inject:<...>` in neatlogs and labelled in the run report. `evidence/recovery/` lists each path with whether its trace was natural or injected.

### 4.6 Budgets and quotas

- **Crustdata:** cap 60 credits per run; never more than 100 credits in one go without asking Akarsh.
- **LLM quota ledger** `cache/ledger.json` (git-ignored): requests and tokens per model per day, against free-tier limits read from AI Studio / OpenRouter in Step 2. A run does not start if remaining quota can't cover it. A client-side rate limiter keeps calls under per-minute limits. `python -m spendradar ledger` prints remaining quota.
- **Caches:** everything cached in development. **Evidence runs** turn the LLM cache off (real model calls) and keep the Crustdata cache on (no re-spend); the report shows each Crustdata response's fetch date. Evidence runs are tagged `evidence` and labelled.

## 6. neatlogs usage (25% category — central, not decorative)

- Install `neatlogs[google-genai]`; call `neatlogs.init(...)` **before** constructing the Gemini client. OpenRouter calls get custom spans (or an instrumentation key if verified in docs).

- Tags are process-wide, so each `spendradar run` is its own process with tags `sha:<short-sha>`, `run:<run_id>`, `variant:<label>`, plus `evidence` / `inject:<...>` / `fixture` when applicable.
- neatlogs has no run-comparison feature we found; our eval scorecards store trace IDs and our table does the comparison. Use neatlogs evals/experiments features only per docs; never invent APIs.

### 6.1 Secret safety

- Client-side `mask` callback in `neatlogs.init(mask=...)`: blank attributes whose key contains key/secret/token/password; regex-mask key formats (`AIza…`, `sk-or-…`, `AKIA…`, `Bearer …`, Crustdata key) in all text values; mask every secret value loaded from `.env`. Do not change server-side PII settings (they are project-wide).
- Unit test: a fake key through a span comes out masked.
- Pre-commit: gitleaks (open source) via `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, appended to Entire's hook, with custom rules for Crustdata and OpenRouter key formats.

## 7. Evals (turn "it improved" into a number)

`ground_truth.json` lists planted errors (mismatched totals, mis-categorised invoice, corrupt file) and correct category totals, plus the fault-injected fixtures.

**Fixtures rule:** Altered fixtures are allowed only in `evals/`, and every run report labels whether it used real data or a fixture. Fixtures in `evals/fixtures/` are cached real Crustdata responses with one field changed on purpose (e.g. ML job postings × 5), each logged in `ground_truth.json`. Product runs only ever read real data. `--fixtures` refuses any folder outside `evals/`, tags the run `fixture`, and sets the report's data mode to FIXTURE.

The eval reports:
- planted errors caught / total
- category total accuracy (abs % error)
- unsupported numbers in report (target 0)
- planted/fixture false findings overturned by self-audit / total (scored)
- competitor findings overturned on real data: N (no ground truth — unscored; report shows both sources side by side)
- title-classifier accuracy on 30 labelled titles (only if used)
- tokens, requests, latency per run, per model; `provider_mix`

**Comparisons:** each side of a before/after = 3 runs with the same provider mix; runs that used fallback are excluded. Report mean and min–max; link one trace per side and list all in the case study. If quota allows fewer than 3, say so — never round up. Check the ledger before starting.

Scorecards → `evidence/evals/<timestamp>-<sha>.json` (including trace IDs); improvement table in `evidence/evals/README.md`.

# cfo.ai inputs: Spend Radar

Akarsh enters these into cfo.ai to build the plan, which must cover **pricing, costs, revenue and runway**. Each line is tagged **MEASURED** (from a real run, with source), **PUBLISHED** (a vendor price, with link and the date I checked it), **PROPOSAL** (a pricing choice we are making), or **ASSUMPTION** (a guess, kept modest and labelled).

## 1. Cost per analysis run

| Input | Value | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLM cost per run (paid-equivalent) | **$0.0285** (range $0.0270–$0.0296) | MEASURED tokens × PUBLISHED prices | `business/unit_costs.md`: 5 evidence runs on gpt-5-nano ($0.05 / $0.40 per 1M tokens), ~30 LLM calls and ~13K in / ~66K out tokens per run. An earlier Gemini Flash run cost $0.0692 (n = 1) |
| Crustdata credits per run, no cache | **20.8 credits** | MEASURED | 5 competitors × 2 credits (enrich) + 360 job results × 0.03 |
| Crustdata USD per credit | **? (to fill)** | PUBLISHED, not public | Crustdata sells credits in the dashboard: https://app.crustdata.com/billing/credits |
| Hosting, one small instance | ≈ $0.0208/h → **≈ $15.2/month** at 730 h | PUBLISHED (third-party) | instances.vantage.sh/aws/ec2/t3.small, checked 2026-10-10. The page does not confirm region and OS; check the AWS console before relying on it |
| Development spend during the hackathon | **$0** to the team | MEASURED | Gemini free tier, OpenRouter `:free`, hackathon-provided OpenAI and Crustdata credits |

Why paid-equivalent: we developed on free tiers, but a paying customer's runs cannot depend on free quotas. The main model is now gpt-5-nano. If we fall back to Gemini Flash, note that its prices rise on 2027-01-01 (3.6/3.8-flash go from $0.75/$3.75 to $1.50/$7.50 per 1M tokens).

## 2. Usage assumptions

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Runs per customer per month | 8 (weekly refresh × 2 scenarios, e.g. budget-cycle what-ifs) | ASSUMPTION |
| Competitors per run | 5 | MEASURED design default |
| Support/onboarding time per new customer | 2 h | ASSUMPTION |

## 3. Proposed pricing tiers (PROPOSAL)

| Tier | Price / month | Includes |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $99 | 1 company, 5 competitors, 8 runs/month, Markdown report |
| Team | $399 | 3 entities, 10 competitors, 40 runs/month, report history, CSV export |
| Enterprise | from $1,500 | SSO, custom policy rules, private deployment (customer data stays off free LLM tiers) |

Per-run variable cost for Starter = 8 × ($0.0285 + 20.8 × Crustdata $/credit). Gross margin depends mainly on the Crustdata credit price, so fill that in first.

## 4. Customer-growth scenarios (ASSUMPTION, deliberately modest)

| Month | Base: paying customers (Starter / Team) | Growth: paying customers (Starter / Team) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | 0 (design partners, free) | 0 |
| 6 | 5 / 1 | 10 / 2 |
| 12 | 15 / 3 | 35 / 8 |
| 24 | 40 / 10 | 100 / 25 |

Churn: 3%/month (base), 2%/month (growth). No market-size (TAM) claims.

## 5. Fixed costs and runway (to fill)

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Founder salary | ? | Akarsh |
| Starting cash | ? | Akarsh |
| Tools/SaaS | neatlogs, Crustdata plan, domain: ? | Akarsh |

The cfo.ai plan should output monthly revenue, COGS (LLM + Crustdata + hosting), gross margin, burn, and months of runway under both scenarios. Export it to `business/` when done.
=====
# Unit costs per run (paid-equivalent estimate)

Generated by `business/compute_unit_costs.py` from evidence runs (LLM cache off). Development spend was **$0** to the team (free tiers and hackathon-provided OpenAI credits). These are the costs a paying deployment would face: **measured tokens × published paid price of the same model**, checked 2026-10-10. Price sources are in the script.

Runs: 5 (target 5).

| Run | Traces | LLM calls | Tokens in / out | Paid-equivalent LLM $ | Crustdata credits (this run / cold) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1010-767322 | `5c512d38b1cc…` | 29 | 12,866 / 65,187 | $0.0279 | 0.0 / 20.8 |
| 1010-bf52d4 | `d4a8716f6d2e…` | 30 | 13,270 / 68,930 | $0.0296 | 0.0 / 20.8 |
| 1010-4d1835 | `0dcf22977776…` | 30 | 13,000 / 67,240 | $0.0290 | 0.0 / 20.8 |
| 1010-bd4980 | `96bb795859c9…` | 30 | 13,847 / 62,274 | $0.0270 | 0.0 / 20.8 |
| 1010-a67b26 | `c4c0b55ade5f…` | 30 | 12,958 / 68,004 | $0.0292 | 0.0 / 20.8 |

**Mean paid-equivalent LLM cost per run: $0.0285** (n=5)
**Mean Crustdata credits per cold run (no cache): 20.80** = 5 competitors × 2 credits + job results × 0.03.

Crustdata does not publish a USD price per credit (docs: credits are bought in the dashboard). **Input needed:** USD per credit from https://app.crustdata.com/billing/credits.


Per model (first run):

| Model | Calls | Tokens in | Tokens out | $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-5-nano | 27 | 11,746 | 64,777 | $0.02650 |
| gemini-3.5-flash-lite | 2 | 1,120 | 410 | $0.00136 |
====
**Confidence is computed, never typed in:** `confidence = checks × signals × freshness` (`spendradar/verify.py`).
- `checks` = passed / total checks behind the finding.
- `signals` = min(1, n_signals / 2) × agreement between signals.
- `freshness` = 1 up to 90 days old, falling to 0.5 at 365 days.
- An audit downgrade halves the score; an overturn sets it to 0.

## How we used the three tools

### neatlogs: tracing is the debugger
- Every Gemini call is auto-traced (`instrumentations=["google_genai"]`). OpenRouter calls, tool calls, `verify:*`, `decide:recovery`, `fallback:<model>`, `audit:<finding>` and `fault:injected:*` are custom spans.
- Runs are tagged `sha:<commit>`, `run:<id>`, `variant:<label>`, `evidence`, `inject:<fault>`, `fixture`. `session_id` = run id, so a resumed run groups with its first trace.
- Secrets are masked client-side before export (`mask=` callback, unit-tested).
- **Every bug fix below started from a trace.** Trace list: [`evidence/traces.md`](evidence/traces.md).

### Entire: context for the coding agent
- Every commit by the coding agent carries an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer that links it to the prompt and transcript behind it. Checkpoints are pushed with the repo.
- `entire graph search` / `impact` were used to locate and size changes, e.g. the callers of `decide_recovery` before changing the recovery menu.
- Evidence: [`evidence/entire/`](evidence/entire/).

### cfo.ai: a business plan from measured costs
- Unit costs are **measured**: tokens per run from evidence runs × the published paid price of the same model. We developed on free tiers, so actual spend was $0.
- Inputs: [`business/inputs.md`](business/inputs.md), [`business/unit_costs.md`](business/unit_costs.md). The cfo.ai plan export goes in `business/`.

## Results so far

All numbers come from scorecards in [`evidence/evals/`](evidence/evals/).

| Run | Commit | Planted errors caught | Unsupported numbers | Peers kept | Crustdata credits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1010-b31657 (before fix) | 11a5108 | 5/5 | 0 | 2/5 | 26.6 |
| 1010-7bf26d (after fix, evidence) | 22f00b0 | 5/5 | 0 | 5/5 | 5.4 |
| 5 evidence runs on gpt-5-nano, 0 fallback hops | bb61e37 | 5/5 in all 5 | 0 | 5/5 | 0 (cached) |
| fixture run (Sentry marketing ×5 planted) | bb61e37 | 6/6 | 0 | 5/5 | 0 (cached) |

Case studies (each n = 1 per side, with caveats stated):
- [01: reasoning calls took ~2 minutes each](evidence/case-studies/01-unbounded-llm-latency.md). Mean reasoning-call latency went from 120.9 s to 6.5 s after adding a per-call timeout with fallback.
- [02: one weak category threw away 3 of 5 peers](evidence/case-studies/02-competitor-substitution.md). Substitutions went from 3 to 0, and credits from 26.6 to 5.4.
- [03: bugs that only showed on fallback models](evidence/case-studies/03-fallback-model-quality.md). Runs that crashed went from 1/3 to 0/3, and the mis-categorised invoice from caught 0/3 to 3/3 on the main model.

Paid-equivalent cost per run (n = 5, gpt-5-nano): **$0.0285 LLM** (range $0.0270–$0.0296) **+ 20.8 Crustdata credits** with no cache.

## Run it yourself

```bash
uv sync                                  # Python 3.12
cp .env.example .env                     # NEATLOGS_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, CRUSTDATA_API_KEY
uv run python scripts/make_acme_data.py  # regenerate the fictional data (already committed)
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme             # full run → runs/<id>/report.md
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme --evidence  # LLM cache off, tagged as evidence
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme --inject crustdata:429 --inject llm:429
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme --crash-after-step 15 && uv run python -m spendradar resume <id>
====

# Building in public — #neatHack (team qwep)

Each entry: draft text, what image to attach, and once posted, the link and timestamp.

---

## Post 1 — the idea + the loop (Sat 10 Oct, ~1 PM IST)

**Status:** draft — not posted

**Text:**

> Building Spend Radar for #neatHack 🛰️
>
> Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They find out a competitor doubled its ML team a quarter too late.
>
> Spend Radar reads a company's budget + invoices, pulls competitor hiring data, and reports where competitors are outspending them on people — with a source behind every number.
>
> The twist: before it reports anything, it tries to disprove its own findings. Claims that don't survive get listed as "overturned", not hidden.
>
> The loop:
> plan → act → verify → (fail? the LLM picks a recovery) → self-audit → report
>
> Every LLM call, tool call, retry and recovery decision traced in @neatlogs. Building with @EntireHQ checkpoints, business plan in cfo.ai.
>
> Solo, 48 hours, all free tiers. Updates as it breaks 👇

**Image:** a clean diagram of the loop (PLAN → ACT → OBSERVE → VERIFY → DECIDE:RECOVERY → SELF-AUDIT → REPORT). It goes in the README too, so draw it once as Mermaid, export it to PNG, and attach that.

**Before posting, check:**
- [ ] The @-handles for Entire and cfo.ai are correct on X (I haven't verified `@EntireHQ`)
- [ ] The repo is public, and adding the link is optional
- [ ] The post contains no numbers that need a source

**Posted:** —  
**Link:** —

---

## Post 2 — first full traced run (Sat 10 Oct, evening)

**Status:** draft — not posted

**Text:**

> First full end-to-end run of Spend Radar for #neatHack, every step traced in @neatlogs.
>
> The agent read a (fictional) company's budget + 13 invoices, pulled real competitor headcount from Crustdata, and wrote a sourced report.
>
> ✅ caught 5/5 errors we planted (bad totals, a mis-filed invoice, a scanned PDF, a corrupt file)
> ✅ 0 numbers in the report without a source
> 🔁 its self-audit overturned its own ML/AI finding: the competitor signals contradicted each other
>
> The traces also caught bugs in *my* agent. One recovery path silently swapped 3 of 5 peer companies for companies 9–32× our size. Fixing that next 👇

**Image:** the report's "Overturned claims" section next to the neatlogs trace for `audit:f_ml_ai` (trace `af0df27e2d3433e0c608fb28a018a22d`).

**Source for every number:** run `1010-b31657`, scorecard `evidence/evals/20261010T141541-11a5108-before-fix.json`. The 9–32× range is Acme’s 330 people (end FY27, budget sheet) vs New Relic (3,095 → 9.4×) and Datadog (10,482 → 31.8×), headcount from Crustdata.

---

## Post 3 — a bug the traces caught (Sun morning)

**Status:** draft — not posted

**Text:**

> #neatHack day 2: the @neatlogs traces caught my agent quietly wrecking its own analysis.
>
> When one competitor's ML/AI estimate was weak, the agent's recovery step *replaced the whole competitor*, dropping its good engineering, sales and marketing data. It did that 3 times. 3 of 5 peers became companies 9–32× our size.
>
> The `decide:recovery` spans showed it plainly: fetch_more_signal (which re-ran the identical cached query, so no new info) → substitute_competitor.
>
> Fix: substitution only when a competitor has *no* data, and "more signal" now fetches a genuinely different sample.
>
> Before → after (1 run each):
> peers kept 2/5 → 5/5
> Crustdata credits 26.6 → 5.4
> planted errors caught 5/5 → 5/5

**Image:** the before trace's `decide:recovery` span list (trace `af0df27e2d3433e0c608fb28a018a22d`) next to the case-study table.

**Sources:** `evidence/case-studies/02-competitor-substitution.md`, scorecards `20261010T141541-11a5108-before-fix.json` and `20261010T141541-22f00b0-after-fix-02.json`.

---

## Post 4 — eval scorecard across commits (Sun afternoon)

**Status:** draft — not posted

**Text:**

> #neatHack: I stopped trusting "it looks better" and made Spend Radar score itself against a ground-truth file the agent never reads. Every run's @neatlogs trace id goes into the scorecard.
>
> Two commits so far:
>
> 11a5108 → 22f00b0
> planted errors caught: 5/5 → 5/5
> unsupported numbers: 0 → 0
> peers kept: 2/5 → 5/5
> Crustdata credits: 26.6 → 5.4
> recovery decisions (non-default): 13 (10) → 10 (7)
>
> Honest caveat: n = 1 per side, both runs used fallback models, and the provider mix differs. So it's indicative, not clean. Same-mix n = 3 runs: {{n3_results}}, after the free-tier quota resets.
>
> Accuracy didn't move. Waste did.

**Image:** the scorecard table from `evidence/evals/README.md`, with the two trace ids visible in the neatlogs dashboard.

**Sources:** `evidence/evals/README.md`, `20261010T141541-11a5108-before-fix.json`, `20261010T141541-22f00b0-after-fix-02.json`.

**Posted:** —  
**Link:** —

---

## Post 5 — self-audit overturning its own claims (Sun night)

**Status:** draft — not posted

**Text:**

> The part of Spend Radar I trust most is the part that argues with it. #neatHack
>
> Before reporting, a self-audit recomputes each finding, checks its sources, and looks for contradictions. An LLM gives a verdict, and a second provider gives an independent opinion.
>
> It overturned the ML/AI finding in runs 1010-b31657 and 1010-a32118 (the competitor signals contradicted each other), and downgraded it in 1010-7bf26d. In a fixture run, a marketing figure disagreed 19 vs 95 and was downgraded.
>
> Then the @neatlogs trace caught a bug in the auditor itself: the "second opinion" used the same model as the first verdict, so it wasn't independent. Fixed: it must now be a different model.
>
> Overturned claims go in the report, not in the bin.
>
> Final scorecard: {{N}} claims caught before reporting.

**Image:** the report's "Overturned claims" section next to the `audit:f_ml_ai` span (trace `af0df27e2d3433e0c608fb28a018a22d`).

**Sources:** `README.md` (Limitations), `evidence/traces.md` (trace `36362eb966cdbb85dcb2fb1b280e1034`, run 1010-9e86fc), commit `15d1109`.

"""Paid-equivalent cost per run, computed from real runs' measured tokens.

Development ran on FREE tiers (actual spend $0). Paying customers cannot rely on free
quotas, so cost = measured tokens per model × the published paid price of the same model.
Only evidence runs (LLM cache off, accounting fix 8747783 or later) are used.
Run: uv run python business/compute_unit_costs.py <run_id> [<run_id> ...]
"""

import json
import statistics
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# USD per 1M tokens (input, output incl. thinking). Checked 2026-10-10.
PRICES = {
    # https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (standard tier), checked 2026-10-10
    "gpt-5-nano": (0.05, 0.40),
    # https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (paid tier, standard)
    "gemini-2.5-flash": (0.30, 2.50),
    "gemini-3.6-flash": (0.75, 3.75),   # rises to 1.50 / 7.50 on 2027-01-01
    "gemini-3.8-flash": (0.75, 3.75),   # rises to 1.50 / 7.50 on 2027-01-01
    "gemini-3.5-flash-lite": (0.30, 2.50),
    "gemini-3.1-flash-lite": (0.25, 1.50),
    # Gemma 4 is free-only on the Gemini API (no paid price listed). PROXY: OpenRouter's paid
    # price for the same model, https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (google/gemma-4-31b-it).
    "gemma-4-31b-it": (0.09, 0.34),
    # https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, the paid (non-:free) variant of the same model
    "nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free": (0.08, 0.45),
    "google/gemma-4-31b-it:free": (0.09, 0.34),
}
CRUSTDATA_LIST = {"enrich_per_company": 2.0, "job_search_per_result": 0.03}  # credits, GET /account/endpoints


def run_cost(run_id: str) -> dict:
    s = json.loads(Path(f"runs/{run_id}/state.json").read_text())
    if "evidence" not in s["tags"]:
        raise SystemExit(f"{run_id} is not an evidence run (LLM cache was on)")
    usd, per_model, unpriced = 0.0, {}, []
    for model, u in s["llm_usage"].items():
        if model not in PRICES:
    if any(r["unpriced_models"] for r in rows):
        out.append(f"Unpriced models (excluded): {sorted({m for r in rows for m in r['unpriced_models']})}")
    out += ["", "Per model (first run):", "", "| Model | Calls | Tokens in | Tokens out | $ |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for m, u in rows[0]["per_model"].items():
        out.append(f"| {m} | {u['calls']} | {u['tokens_in']:,} | {u['tokens_out']:,} | ${u['usd']:.5f} |")
    Path("business/unit_costs.md").write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")
    Path("business/unit_costs.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=1))
    print("\n".join(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

# cfo.ai inputs: Spend Radar

Akarsh enters these into cfo.ai to build the plan, which must cover **pricing, costs, revenue and runway**. Each line is tagged **MEASURED** (from a real run, with source), **PUBLISHED** (a vendor price, with link and the date I checked it), **PROPOSAL** (a pricing choice we are making), or **ASSUMPTION** (a guess, kept modest and labelled).

## 1. Cost per analysis run

| Input | Value | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLM cost per run (paid-equivalent) | **$0.0285** (range $0.0270–$0.0296) | MEASURED tokens × PUBLISHED prices | `business/unit_costs.md`: 5 evidence runs on gpt-5-nano ($0.05 / $0.40 per 1M tokens), ~30 LLM calls and ~13K in / ~66K out tokens per run. An earlier Gemini Flash run cost $0.0692 (n = 1) |
| Crustdata credits per run, no cache | **20.8 credits** | MEASURED | 5 competitors × 2 credits (enrich) + 360 job results × 0.03 |
| Crustdata USD per credit | **? (to fill)** | PUBLISHED, not public | Crustdata sells credits in the dashboard: https://app.crustdata.com/billing/credits |
| Hosting, one small instance | ≈ $0.0208/h → **≈ $15.2/month** at 730 h | PUBLISHED (third-party) | instances.vantage.sh/aws/ec2/t3.small, checked 2026-10-10. The page does not confirm region and OS; check the AWS console before relying on it |
| Development spend during the hackathon | **$0** to the team | MEASURED | Gemini free tier, OpenRouter `:free`, hackathon-provided OpenAI and Crustdata credits |

Why paid-equivalent: we developed on free tiers, but a paying customer's runs cannot depend on free quotas. The main model is now gpt-5-nano. If we fall back to Gemini Flash, note that its prices rise on 2027-01-01 (3.6/3.8-flash go from $0.75/$3.75 to $1.50/$7.50 per 1M tokens).

## 2. Usage assumptions

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Runs per customer per month | 8 (weekly refresh × 2 scenarios, e.g. budget-cycle what-ifs) | ASSUMPTION |
| Competitors per run | 5 | MEASURED design default |
| Support/onboarding time per new customer | 2 h | ASSUMPTION |

## 3. Proposed pricing tiers (PROPOSAL)

| Tier | Price / month | Includes |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $99 | 1 company, 5 competitors, 8 runs/month, Markdown report |
| Team | $399 | 3 entities, 10 competitors, 40 runs/month, report history, CSV export |
| Enterprise | from $1,500 | SSO, custom policy rules, private deployment (customer data stays off free LLM tiers) |

Per-run variable cost for Starter = 8 × ($0.0285 + 20.8 × Crustdata $/credit). Gross margin depends mainly on the Crustdata credit price, so fill that in first.

| Month | Base: paying customers (Starter / Team) | Growth: paying customers (Starter / Team) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | 0 (design partners, free) | 0 |
| 6 | 5 / 1 | 10 / 2 |
| 12 | 15 / 3 | 35 / 8 |
| 24 | 40 / 10 | 100 / 25 |

Churn: 3%/month (base), 2%/month (growth). No market-size (TAM) claims.

## 5. Fixed costs and runway (to fill)

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Founder salary | ? | Akarsh |
| Starting cash | ? | Akarsh |
| Tools/SaaS | neatlogs, Crustdata plan, domain: ? | Akarsh |

The cfo.ai plan should output monthly revenue, COGS (LLM + Crustdata + hosting), gross margin, burn, and months of runway under both scenarios. Export it to `business/` when done.

# cfo.ai inputs: Spend Radar

Akarsh enters these into cfo.ai to build the plan, which must cover **pricing, costs, revenue and runway**. Each line is tagged **MEASURED** (from a real run, with source), **PUBLISHED** (a vendor price, with link and the date I checked it), **PROPOSAL** (a pricing choice we are making), or **ASSUMPTION** (a guess, kept modest and labelled).

## 1. Cost per analysis run

| Input | Value | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLM cost per run (paid-equivalent) | **$0.0285** (range $0.0270–$0.0296) | MEASURED tokens × PUBLISHED prices | `business/unit_costs.md`: 5 evidence runs on gpt-5-nano ($0.05 / $0.40 per 1M tokens), ~30 LLM calls and ~13K in / ~66K out tokens per run. An earlier Gemini Flash run cost $0.0692 (n = 1) |
| Crustdata credits per run, no cache | **20.8 credits** | MEASURED | 5 competitors × 2 credits (enrich) + 360 job results × 0.03 |
| Crustdata USD per run, no cache | **$6.24–$9.24** | MEASURED usage × PUBLISHED dashboard prices | Crustdata billing page (pay-as-you-go, screenshot 2026-10-10): Company Enrich $0.60–$1.20 per record, Search (person, company, jobs) $9.00 per 1k records. 5 enriches = $3.00–$6.00; 360 job results = $3.24. Implies ≈ $0.30–$0.60 per credit. Assumes each job result is billed as one search record |
| Hosting, one small instance | ≈ $0.0208/h → **≈ $15.2/month** at 730 h | PUBLISHED (third-party) | instances.vantage.sh/aws/ec2/t3.small, checked 2026-10-10. The page does not confirm region and OS; check the AWS console before relying on it |
| Development spend during the hackathon | **$0** to the team | MEASURED | Gemini free tier, OpenRouter `:free`, hackathon-provided OpenAI and Crustdata credits |

Why paid-equivalent: we developed on free tiers, but a paying customer's runs cannot depend on free quotas. The main model is now gpt-5-nano. If we fall back to Gemini Flash, note that its prices rise on 2027-01-01 (3.6/3.8-flash go from $0.75/$3.75 to $1.50/$7.50 per 1M tokens).

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|

Per-run variable cost for Starter = 8 × ($0.0285 + 20.8 × Crustdata $/credit). Gross margin depends mainly on the Crustdata credit price, so fill that in first.

| Month | Base: paying customers (Starter / Team) | Growth: paying customers (Starter / Team) |
|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | 0 (design partners, free) | 0 |
| 6 | 5 / 1 | 10 / 2 |
| 12 | 15 / 3 | 35 / 8 |
| 24 | 40 / 10 | 100 / 25 |

Churn: 3%/month (base), 2%/month (growth). No market-size (TAM) claims.

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Founder salary | ? | Akarsh |
| Starting cash | ? | Akarsh |
| Tools/SaaS | neatlogs, Crustdata plan, domain: ? | Akarsh |
