             fixtures: str | None = None, data: str = "data/acme") -> Path:
    run_ids = list(score_only or [])
    for _ in range(0 if score_only else n):
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "spendradar", "run", data, "--variant", variant]
        cmd += ["--evidence"] if evidence else []
        cmd += ["--fixtures", fixtures] if fixtures else []
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        m = re.search(r'"run_id": "([^"]+)"', out.stdout)
        if not m:
            print(out.stdout[-2000:], out.stderr[-2000:])
            raise SystemExit("run failed to start")
        run_ids.append(m.group(1))
    scores = [score_run(r) for r in run_ids]
    no_fallback = [s for s in scores if s["fallback_hops"] == 0]
    keys = ("planted_caught", "false_alarms", "unsupported_numbers_in_report", "overturned", "downgraded", "recovery_decisions",
            "llm_calls", "llm_tokens_in", "llm_tokens_out", "llm_latency_s", "crustdata_credits")
    card = {
        "created": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "variant": variant, "evidence": evidence,
        "git_sha": scores[0]["git_sha"] if scores else "", "n_runs": len(scores),
        "n_runs_without_fallback": len(no_fallback),
        "planted_total": scores[0]["planted_total"] if scores else 0,
        "summary_all_runs": {k: _agg([s[k] for s in scores]) for k in keys} if scores else {},
        "summary_no_fallback_runs": {k: _agg([s[k] for s in no_fallback]) for k in keys} if no_fallback else {},
        "runs": scores,
    }
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = OUT / f"{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')}-{card['git_sha']}-{variant}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(card, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    return path

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. ALWAYS call search_design_system first to find existing components, variables, and styles to reuse — never generate components from scratch if a design system match exists.
3. For web app pages, use both tools in parallel: generate_figma_design to capture a pixel-perfect screenshot, and use_figma to build the screen from imported design system components. Refine use_figma output against the screenshot, then delete the screenshot reference.
4. For non-web targets (iOS, Android, generic UI), use use_figma with search_design_system.
5. For updating or syncing a Figma page that has already been captured, use use_figma — even if the source code has changed.

FROM-SCRATCH DESIGN WORKFLOW (no source design or code):

Use this MCP to deploy, manage, and debug applications on Railway. Call the direct tools for reads and routine operations — listing projects/services/variables/domains, inspecting config, status, logs, metrics, setting variables, updating service settings, creating services, and searching the Railway docs. Reach for the `railway-agent` tool when a task is genuinely complex or open-ended (multi-service debugging, incident investigation, operations that span many steps or need Railway-side reasoning). Fall back to the local Railway CLI when needed. Confirm with the user before destructive actions (e.g. `accept-deploy`).

## claude.ai Vercel
Use Vercel tools and their input schemas.

Reuse supplied or discovered IDs and connection scope; never guess. If scope is unknown, discover teams then projects. Ask only if the target stays ambiguous.

If MCP fails or lacks an operation, use CLI fallbacks in error results, tool descriptions and _meta["vercel.com/cli"]. Run templates with inputs/scope; CLI auth differs; skip whoami/team probes. Help only for unmapped options or usage errors. Save secrets privately (umask 077); never print secrets.

For vercel api, URL-encode paths; query in URL (repeat array keys; omit null), headers via --header, body via --input JSON object file, not -F. Preserve schema defaults/coercions and pagination; auth/output differ.

Inspect deployment state/logs before changes. For visuals, use open_deployments if available. Search docs as needed.

Filter reads by project, time and supported fields. Follow pagination for complete lists; state partial or truncated results. Batch independent calls; wait before dependent calls.

Read only state needed for the change; verify afterward. For domain purchases, present get_purchase_quote pricing and disclosures for explicit approval, then use buy_domain with confirm:true and its quote token. Subscriptions, credits and add-ons are unavailable. Never request credentials or private keys; use connection/resource IDs. Never decrypt environment values unless requested.

Inspect every result, including batch failures. Correct invalid inputs using the schema. For access or not-found errors, verify scope; not-found does not always mean no access. Retry transient failures only when safe; check state before retrying writes with uncertain outcomes. Distinguish pending from completed work. For requires_user_action, present the dashboard URL for the user to finish; do not bypass it or claim completion.

"""CLI: python -m spendradar run|resume|ledger …  (one process = one neatlogs-tagged run)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

from dotenv import load_dotenv


def _start(run_id: str, args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[str]:
    from spendradar import faults
    from spendradar.tracing import init_tracing

    if args.evidence:
        os.environ["SPENDRADAR_LLM_CACHE"] = "0"
    if args.fixtures:
        from pathlib import Path

        from spendradar.tools import crustdata

        if not Path(args.fixtures).resolve().is_relative_to(Path("evals").resolve()):
            raise SystemExit("fixtures are only allowed from evals/")
        crustdata.FIXTURE_DIR = Path(args.fixtures)
    faults.configure(args.inject or [])
    tags = [f"variant:{args.variant}"] + (["evidence"] if args.evidence else [])
    tags += ["fixture"] if args.fixtures else []
    tags += [f"inject:{i}" for i in args.inject or []]
    return init_tracing(run_id, tags)


def _finish(state) -> None:
    from spendradar.tracing import shutdown_tracing

    shutdown_tracing()
    print(json.dumps({"run_id": state.run_id, "phase": state.phase, "trace_id": state.trace_id,
                      "trace_ids": state.trace_ids,
                      "report": f"runs/{state.run_id}/report.md", "findings": [
                          {"id": f.id, "status": f.status, "confidence": f.confidence} for f in state.findings],
                      "decisions": [(d.task_id, d.chosen, d.default) for d in state.decisions],
                      "llm_usage": state.llm_usage, "crustdata_credits": state.crustdata_credits}, indent=1))


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    load_dotenv(".env")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="spendradar")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    for name in ("run", "resume"):
        p = sub.add_parser(name)
        p.add_argument("target", help="input folder (run) or run id (resume)")
        p.add_argument("--inject", action="append", help="fault to inject, e.g. crustdata:429, llm:429")
        p.add_argument("--variant", default="dev")
        p.add_argument("--evidence", action="store_true", help="LLM cache off; tagged as an evidence run")
        p.add_argument("--crash-after-step", type=int, default=None, help="simulate a crash (resume demo)")
        p.add_argument("--fixtures", default=None, help="EVALS ONLY: folder of altered Crustdata fixtures")
    sub.add_parser("ledger")
    e = sub.add_parser("eval")
    e.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=1)
    e.add_argument("--variant", default="eval")
    e.add_argument("--evidence", action="store_true")
    e.add_argument("--score", nargs="*", help="score existing run ids instead of launching runs")
    e.add_argument("--fixtures", default=None, help="EVALS ONLY: run against altered fixtures")
    e.add_argument("--data", default="data/acme", help="input folder, e.g. data/kestrel (held-out)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd == "ledger":
        from spendradar import llm

        print(json.dumps(llm.LEDGER.summary(), indent=1))
        return

    if args.cmd == "eval":
        from spendradar import evals

        path = evals.run_eval(args.n, args.variant, args.evidence, args.score, args.fixtures, args.data)
        card = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        print(f"scorecard: {path}")
        print(json.dumps({k: card[k] for k in ("n_runs", "n_runs_without_fallback", "planted_total",
                                                "summary_all_runs")}, indent=1))
        return

    from spendradar import agent  # noqa: F401  (imported after env is ready)

    if args.cmd == "run":
        run_id = agent.new_run_id()
        tags = _start(run_id, args)
        from spendradar.tracing import git_sha

        state = agent.new_state(args.target, tags, git_sha(), run_id)
        agent.save(state)
    else:
        state = agent.load(args.target)
        _start(state.run_id, args)
        state.notes.append(f"resumed at phase '{state.phase}', step {state.step}")
    if args.crash_after_step:
        agent.CRASH_AFTER_STEP = args.crash_after_step
    try:
        state = agent.run_phases(state)
    finally:
        _finish(state)
    sys.exit(0 if state.phase == "done" else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Export every scored run as one JSON file for a front end: evidence/frontend_data.json.

`python -m spendradar export` reads evidence/evals/*.json (committed scorecards) and, when present,
runs/<id>/state.json (local), and writes a stable structure documented in docs/frontend-data.md.
Every value is copied from a scorecard, a run's state or a ground-truth file; nothing is computed here
except counts. Bump SCHEMA_VERSION when a field changes meaning.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
EVALS = Path("evidence/evals")
OUT = Path("evidence/frontend_data.json")

LABELS = {
    "budget_total_mismatch": "Budget row total does not equal the sum of its months",
    "invoice_total_mismatch": "Invoice line items do not add up to the stated total",
    "invoice_miscategorised": "Invoice billed to the wrong cost centre",
    "invoice_miscategorised_single_vendor": "Invoice billed to the wrong cost centre (vendor appears once)",
    "invoice_scanned": "Scanned invoice with no text layer",
    "invoice_corrupt": "Corrupt or empty PDF",
    "invoice_duplicate": "Same invoice sent twice",
    "fixture_sentry_marketing_x5": "Eval fixture: a competitor's headcount altered ×5",
}


def _company(dataset: str) -> dict:
    truth = Path("evals/ground_truth.json" if dataset == "acme" else f"evals/ground_truth_{dataset}.json")
    t = json.loads(truth.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if truth.exists() else {}
    comps_path = Path(f"data/{dataset}/competitors.yaml")
    comps = yaml.safe_load(comps_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if comps_path.exists() else {}
    return {
        "key": dataset,
        "name": t.get("company", "Acme Observability Inc." if dataset == "acme" else dataset),
        "industry": t.get("industry", "observability SaaS" if dataset == "acme" else ""),
        "role": "development" if dataset == "acme" else "held_out",
        "fictional": True,
        "competitors": [{"name": c["name"], "domain": c["domain"]} for c in comps.get("competitors", [])],
        "negative_controls": [p["id"] for p in t.get("planted_errors", []) if p and p["type"] == "negative_control"],
        "runs": [],
    }


def _run(r: dict, card: dict, path: Path) -> dict:
    st_path = Path(f"runs/{r['run_id']}/state.json")
    st = json.loads(st_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if st_path.exists() else None
    out = {
        "run_id": r["run_id"], "variant": card.get("variant", ""), "scored_at": card.get("created", ""),
        "git_sha": r["git_sha"], "neatlogs_trace_id": r["trace_id"], "scorecard": path.as_posix(),
        "data_mode": r.get("data_mode", "real"), "injected_faults": r.get("injected", []),
        "metrics": {
            "planted_caught": r["planted_caught"], "planted_total": r["planted_total"],
            "false_alarms": r.get("false_alarms"),  # null on scorecards written before false alarms were counted
            "unsupported_numbers_in_report": r["unsupported_numbers_in_report"],
            "findings_overturned": r["overturned"], "findings_downgraded": r["downgraded"],
            "recovery_decisions": r["recovery_decisions"], "recovery_non_default": r["recovery_non_default"],
            "llm_calls": r["llm_calls"], "llm_tokens_in": r["llm_tokens_in"], "llm_tokens_out": r["llm_tokens_out"],
            "llm_latency_s": r["llm_latency_s"], "fallback_hops": r.get("fallback_hops", 0),
            "crustdata_credits": round(r["crustdata_credits"], 2), "models": r.get("provider_mix", []),
        },
        "planted": [{"id": k, "label": LABELS.get(k, k), "caught": v} for k, v in r["planted_detail"].items()],
        "false_alarm_detail": r.get("false_alarm_detail", []),
        "report": {"markdown": f"runs/{r['run_id']}/report.md", "html": f"runs/{r['run_id']}/report.html",
                   "available_locally": st is not None},
        "findings": [], "recovery": [],
    }
    if st:
        out["findings"] = [{"id": f["id"], "category": f["category"], "kind": f["kind"], "status": f["status"],
                            "confidence": f["confidence"], "statement": f["statement"],
                            "policy_violated": f.get("policy_violated"), "audit_notes": f.get("audit_notes", [])}
                           for f in st["findings"]]
        out["recovery"] = [{"task_id": d["task_id"], "chosen": d["chosen"], "rule_default": d["default"],
                            "reason": d.get("reason", "")} for d in st.get("decisions", [])]
    return out


def build() -> Path:
    companies: dict[str, dict] = {}
    latest: dict[str, tuple[dict, dict, Path]] = {}
    for p in sorted(EVALS.glob("2026*.json")):
        card = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for r in card.get("runs", []):
            if "planted_detail" in r:
                latest[r["run_id"]] = (r, card, p)  # a run scored twice keeps its latest scorecard
    for r, card, p in sorted(latest.values(), key=lambda x: x[1].get("created", "")):
        ds = r.get("dataset") or "acme"
        companies.setdefault(ds, _company(ds))["runs"].append(_run(r, card, p))
    order = ["acme"] + sorted(k for k in companies if k != "acme")
    data = {"schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION, "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
            "companies": [companies[k] for k in order if k in companies],
            "business": {"plan": "business/cfoai_plan.md", "unit_costs": "business/unit_costs.md",
                         "cfoai_exports": "business/cfoai/"}}
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    return OUT

# Front-end data format

The front end reads one file: `evidence/frontend_data.json`. Regenerate it after any eval with:

```bash
uv run python -m spendradar export
```

Every value is copied from a scorecard (`evidence/evals/*.json`), a run's state (`runs/<id>/state.json`, local only) or a ground-truth file. The front end should display these values, not recompute them. All company finance data is fictional; competitors are real companies with data from Crustdata.

## Top level

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | int | Bumped when a field changes meaning. Currently `1`. |
| `generated_at` | ISO datetime | When the export ran. |
| `companies` | Company[] | Acme first (the development set), then held-out companies A–Z. |
| `business` | object | Paths to the cfo.ai plan (`plan`), unit costs (`unit_costs`) and the cfo.ai exports folder (`cfoai_exports`). |

## Company

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Folder name under `data/`, e.g. `ledgerly`. |
| `name` | string | e.g. `Ledgerly Payments Inc.` |
| `industry` | string | e.g. `fintech (spend management)` |
| `role` | `"development"` \| `"held_out"` | Acme is the company the agent was built against. Held-out companies were never used to tune it. |
| `fictional` | bool | Always `true`; show a "fictional data" label. |
| `competitors` | {name, domain}[] | Real peers the agent compares against. |
| `negative_controls` | string[] | Planted items the agent must NOT flag (e.g. a 0.4% rounding difference). A flag on one counts as a false alarm. |
| `runs` | Run[] | Oldest first. The last one is the current state. |

## Run

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | e.g. `1010-d514dc` |
| `variant` | string | Label for what was being tested, e.g. `baseline-kestrel`, `after-heldout-fixes-kestrel`. Use it to pair before/after. |
| `scored_at` | ISO datetime | When the scorecard was written. |
| `git_sha` | string | Commit the run used. A `-dirty` suffix means uncommitted changes were present. |
| `neatlogs_trace_id` | string | Searchable in the neatlogs dashboard (app.neatlogs.com). |
| `scorecard` | path | The JSON this run was copied from. |
| `data_mode` | `"real"` \| `"fixture"` | `fixture` = altered competitor data, eval only. Must be shown prominently. |
| `injected_faults` | string[] | Faults deliberately injected (e.g. `crustdata:429`); empty for normal runs. |
| `metrics` | object | See below. |
| `planted` | {id, label, caught}[] | Each planted error and whether this run caught it. Good for a ✓/✗ grid. |
| `false_alarm_detail` | string[] | What the agent flagged that the ground truth says is fine. |
| `report` | {markdown, html, available_locally} | Paths to the run's full report. `runs/` is not committed, so `available_locally` is false on other machines. |
| `findings` | Finding[] | Empty unless the run's state is available locally. |
| `recovery` | Recovery[] | Each recovery decision; empty unless state is local. |

### `metrics`

`planted_caught`, `planted_total`, `false_alarms` (null on older scorecards that predate the count), `unsupported_numbers_in_report` (target 0), `findings_overturned`, `findings_downgraded`, `recovery_decisions`, `recovery_non_default` (the LLM chose something other than the fixed rule's default), `llm_calls`, `llm_tokens_in`, `llm_tokens_out`, `llm_latency_s`, `fallback_hops` (runs with >0 are excluded from clean before/after comparisons), `crustdata_credits` (0 when served from cache), `models`.

### Finding

`id`, `category` (engineering, ml_ai, sales, marketing, infra_cloud, internal), `kind` (`policy` = vs competitors, `internal` = own books, `gap`), `status` (`confirmed`, `downgraded`, `overturned` — overturned findings are not in the report and belong in an "agent disproved itself" view), `confidence` (0–1, computed; formula in `spendradar/verify.py`), `statement`, `policy_violated`, `audit_notes` (the self-audit's reasoning, including second opinions).

### Recovery

`task_id`, `chosen`, `rule_default`, `reason`. Highlight rows where `chosen != rule_default`: those are the LLM's own decisions.

## Suggested views (for the design, not prescriptive)

1. **Generalisation table**: one row per company, first vs latest run (`planted_caught/planted_total`, `false_alarms`).
2. **Run detail**: metrics tiles, the planted ✓/✗ grid, findings grouped by status, the recovery list, trace id.
3. **Overturned claims**: findings with `status = overturned` or `downgraded`, with `audit_notes`.
4. **Business**: link to `business/cfoai_plan.md`; the numbers there are from cfo.ai and are not in this file.

| `business` | object | Paths to the cfo.ai plan (`plan`), unit costs (`unit_costs`) and the cfo.ai exports folder (`cfoai_exports`). |

## Company

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Folder name under `data/`, e.g. `ledgerly`. |
| `name` | string | e.g. `Ledgerly Payments Inc.` |
| `industry` | string | e.g. `fintech (spend management)` |
| `role` | `"development"` \| `"held_out"` | Acme is the company the agent was built against. Held-out companies were never used to tune it. |
| `fictional` | bool | Always `true`; show a "fictional data" label. |
| `competitors` | {name, domain}[] | Real peers the agent compares against. |
| `negative_controls` | string[] | Planted items the agent must NOT flag (e.g. a 0.4% rounding difference). A flag on one counts as a false alarm. |
| `runs` | Run[] | Oldest first. The last one is the current state. |

## Run

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | string | e.g. `1010-d514dc` |
| `variant` | string | Label for what was being tested, e.g. `baseline-kestrel`, `after-heldout-fixes-kestrel`. Use it to pair before/after. |
| `scored_at` | ISO datetime | When the scorecard was written. |
| `git_sha` | string | Commit the run used. A `-dirty` suffix means uncommitted changes were present. |
| `neatlogs_trace_id` | string | Searchable in the neatlogs dashboard (app.neatlogs.com). |
| `scorecard` | path | The JSON this run was copied from. |
| `data_mode` | `"real"` \| `"fixture"` | `fixture` = altered competitor data, eval only. Must be shown prominently. |
| `injected_faults` | string[] | Faults deliberately injected (e.g. `crustdata:429`); empty for normal runs. |
| `metrics` | object | See below. |
| `planted` | {id, label, caught}[] | Each planted error and whether this run caught it. Good for a ✓/✗ grid. |
| `false_alarm_detail` | string[] | What the agent flagged that the ground truth says is fine. |
| `report` | {markdown, html, available_locally} | Paths to the run's full report. `runs/` is not committed, so `available_locally` is false on other machines. |
| `findings` | Finding[] | Empty unless the run's state is available locally. |
| `recovery` | Recovery[] | Each recovery decision; empty unless state is local. |

### `metrics`

`planted_caught`, `planted_total`, `false_alarms` (null on older scorecards that predate the count), `unsupported_numbers_in_report` (target 0), `findings_overturned`, `findings_downgraded`, `recovery_decisions`, `recovery_non_default` (the LLM chose something other than the fixed rule's default), `llm_calls`, `llm_tokens_in`, `llm_tokens_out`, `llm_latency_s`, `fallback_hops` (runs with >0 are excluded from clean before/after comparisons), `crustdata_credits` (0 when served from cache), `models`.

### Finding

`id`, `category` (engineering, ml_ai, sales, marketing, infra_cloud, internal), `kind` (`policy` = vs competitors, `internal` = own books, `gap`), `status` (`confirmed`, `downgraded`, `overturned` — overturned findings are not in the report and belong in an "agent disproved itself" view), `confidence` (0–1, computed; formula in `spendradar/verify.py`), `statement`, `policy_violated`, `audit_notes` (the self-audit's reasoning, including second opinions).

### Recovery

`task_id`, `chosen`, `rule_default`, `reason`. Highlight rows where `chosen != rule_default`: those are the LLM's own decisions.

## Suggested views (for the design, not prescriptive)

1. **Generalisation table**: one row per company, first vs latest run (`planted_caught/planted_total`, `false_alarms`).
2. **Run detail**: metrics tiles, the planted ✓/✗ grid, findings grouped by status, the recovery list, trace id.
3. **Overturned claims**: findings with `status = overturned` or `downgraded`, with `audit_notes`.
4. **Business**: link to `business/cfoai_plan.md`; the numbers there are from cfo.ai and are not in this file.

They run one after another once Ledgerly and Acme finish. Each will spend about 11–25 Crustdata credits, based on the runs so far. Expect them all to finish in about an hour.

The full prompts are in **[business/cfoai_prompts_round2.md](SpeedRadar-NeetHack/business/cfoai_prompts_round2.md)**, ready to paste. They follow up the next steps Ari suggested in round 1, using costs measured in these runs:

- Posts and the demo video are still the biggest gaps for scoring.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Spend Radar business plan (built in cfo.ai)

The plan was built by Ari, cfo.ai's AI CFO, from [`cfoai_prompt.md`](cfoai_prompt.md). It covers **pricing, costs, revenue and runway** over 24 months (Nov 2026 to Oct 2028), with a Base scenario and a Growth scenario.

Exports from cfo.ai, in [`cfoai/`](cfoai/):
- [`Summary.xlsx`](cfoai/Summary.xlsx): Base vs Growth, month by month
- [`Monthly P&L & Cash.xlsx`](cfoai/Monthly%20P%26L%20%26%20Cash.xlsx): customers, runs, revenue, COGS, burn, cash, runway (Base)
- [`Unit Economics.xlsx`](cfoai/Unit%20Economics.xlsx): per-customer economics and cache sensitivity
- [`Assumptions.xlsx`](cfoai/Assumptions.xlsx): every input

**Cross-check:** [`make_cfoai_sheet.py`](make_cfoai_sheet.py) rebuilds the model independently in Python. Across all 24 months of both scenarios, its customers, revenue, net burn and ending cash match the cfo.ai export to within $0.01. The first comparison turned up one difference: Python's `round()` rounds 22.5 down to 22, while cfo.ai rounds it up to 23. The script now rounds half up.

## Where the inputs come from

| Input | Value | Type |
|---|---|---|
| LLM cost per run | $0.0285 | MEASURED: mean of 5 evidence runs × the model's published paid price ([`unit_costs.md`](unit_costs.md)) |
| Crustdata cost per run, no cache | $9.24 (Base) / $6.24 (Growth) | MEASURED usage (5 company enrich calls, 360 job results) × PUBLISHED Crustdata prices ($0.60–$1.20 per enrich, $9 per 1,000 search records) |
| Share of runs served from cache | 50% | ASSUMPTION (not yet measured) |
| Hosting | $15.20/month | PUBLISHED (third-party price for one t3.small instance) |
| Pricing | Starter $99 (8 runs), Team $399 (40 runs) | PROPOSAL |
| Customers | Base 40 Starter / 10 Team by month 24; Growth 100 / 25 | ASSUMPTION (counts are net of churn) |
| Founder salary, tools, starting cash | $2,000/month, $100/month, $25,000 | SAMPLE placeholders |

## Results

| | Base | Growth |
|---|---|---|
| First cash-flow-positive month | Jan 2028 (month 15, +$248) | Jun 2027 (month 8, +$306) |
| Lowest cash balance | $7,149 (Dec 2027) | $14,615 (May 2027) |
| Revenue in month 24 | $7,950 | $19,875 |
| Gross margin in month 24 | 57.7% | 71.4% |
| Cash in month 24 | $20,739 | $115,486 |

### Unit economics per customer per month (Base, 50% of runs cached)

| Tier | Revenue | Cost to serve | Gross margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $99 | $37.19 | 62.4% |
| Team | $399 | $185.94 | 53.5% |

Growth (cheaper Crustdata enrich): Starter 74.6%, Team 68.4%.

### Cache sensitivity (gross margin, 0% vs 50% of runs cached)

| Tier | Base, 0% | Base, 50% | Growth, 0% | Growth, 50% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | 25.1% | 62.4% | 49.3% | 74.6% |
| Team | 7.1% | 53.5% | 37.2% | 68.4% |

## What the plan tells us

1. **Crustdata is about 99% of the cost of serving a customer.** LLM inference is $0.0285 a run. Over 24 months Crustdata costs $33.4k in Base and $55.7k in Growth; founder salary costs $48k.
2. **Caching competitor data is the business.** Without it, Team keeps 7% of its revenue in Base. The agent already caches Crustdata responses per run. The next step is to share one fetch across customers who track the same competitors, and to measure the real cache hit rate.
3. **Team is priced wrong.** It gets 5× the runs for 4× the price, so its margin is below Starter's. Options: raise its price, or cap the runs that need fresh competitor data.
4. **Base is tight.** The cash low of $7.1k is about 3 months of the $2.1k monthly burn, so customers arriving 2–3 months late would run Base out of cash.

## Limits

- The salary, tools and starting cash are placeholders, not real figures.
- The 50% cache rate is an assumption. It has not been measured.
- Customer counts are assumptions, deliberately modest, with no market-size claims.
- The Crustdata cost assumes each job-search result is billed as one search record.

content.content:
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

Usage:
  entire session attach <session-id> [flags]

Flags:
